diagnostics.message: The `$default` stage is created with `auto_deploy = true`, but it only depends on `aws_apigatewayv2_api.webhook` — nothing orders it after the route/integration. The provider snapshots the routes that exist at stage-creation time, so if the stage's initial deployment runs before `aws_apigatewayv2_route.webhook` (which in turn requires `aws_apigatewayv2_integration.webhook`) exists, the deployed API has no `POST /webhook` route and the webhook endpoint returns 404. `aws_apigatewayv2_stage.webhook` should depend on `aws_apigatewayv2_route.webhook` (this is operational ordering, not inferable from any attribute).

`null_resource.update_app` calls `update-app.sh` with `var.webhook_endpoint`, which is built from `module.webhook.gateway.api_endpoint` (an attribute of `aws_apigatewayv2_api.webhook`) rather than from the deployed stage. That value is available as soon as the API resource exists, so Terraform may run the GitHub App update before the API Gateway stage/route are actually deployed. The app then points at an endpoint that 404s until the stage exists. The updater should depend on the webhook's stage (which transitively follows route → integration → lambda) so the endpoint is live before it is registered.
